Title: Diagnosis of test `testExcelHeaderCountLessThanData`
Details: The test method `testExcelHeaderCountLessThanData` creates a CSV input string with a header row "A,B,C,," and a data row "a,b,c,d,e". It then attempts to parse this using `CSVParser.parse` with the `CSVFormat.EXCEL.withHeader()` setting.

`CSVFormat.EXCEL` inherits mostly default settings but disables ignoring empty lines. The `withHeader()` method called without arguments sets the header to an empty array, implying the parser should read the first record line as the header line automatically (`formatHeader.length == 0`).

Looking at the `CSVParser` constructor and `initializeHeader()`, the parser reads the first record to set up header columns from it. The header row contains five columns including two trailing empty ones. The data row contains five columns with non-empty values. The header map is built from the first record.

The problem is the header row contains empty headers. The code in `initializeHeader()` checks if headers are empty (null or whitespace) and whether missing column names are allowed (`allowMissingColumnNames`). If empty headers are not allowed, it may raise exceptions or cause faulty mapping. Also, the header count is less than the data count but the parser likely does not handle the mismatch gracefully.

As the test failed, the root cause appears to be the handling of the header count being less than data columns and how empty header columns are processed in this scenario, leading to an error or unexpected behavior during parsing.

Suggested fix locations are in `CSVParser.initializeHeader()` and related header empty column handling logic in the parser. Possibly also review the `CSVFormat` configuration for `allowMissingColumnNames`.

Next, I will check `allowMissingColumnNames` usage and default in `CSVFormat`.
